# SECflow — full brief for AI coding agents

SECflow (npm package `secflow`) is a zero-dependency, single-file security scanner for repos written by/with AI coding agents. It unifies gitleaks (secrets), trivy (dep/container CVEs, opt-in), `npm audit`, and custom regex rules into one report with AI-ready fix briefs. MIT licensed. Node >= 18.

## Commands (user-facing)

```
secflow scan [--path DIR] [--skip gitleaks,trivy,npm,regex] [--fail-on critical,high] [--json]
secflow report [--path DIR]        # print last scan's AI-ready brief (.secflow/report.md)
secflow init [--path DIR]          # write secflow.yml
secflow install-hook [--path DIR]  # pre-commit hook → gitleaks --staged
secflow ci [--path DIR] [--skip …] [--fail-on …]   # CI mode, exit 1 when blocked
```

Exit codes: 0 = clean, 1 = findings at/above failOn, 2 = internal error.

## Architecture

Everything is `bin/secflow.js`. Flow: parse args → load `secflow.yml` over DEFAULT_CONFIG → run enabled engines (gitleaks, trivy, npm audit, regex walker) → dedupe by engine|file|line|rule → write `.secflow/report.md` + `report.json` → exit per failOn.

- Config parsing is a deliberate YAML subset: flat keys, `engines.*`, `failOn`, `excludePaths` (comma list), `customRegex.<name>: { pattern: '…', severity: … }`.
- `excludePaths` entries get trailing slashes normalized before comparison (dir-name match).
- CLI `--fail-on` overrides yml `failOn`; applies to both `scan` and `ci` via `applyCliFailOn()`.
- Regex engine always re-adds `.git`, `node_modules`, `.secflow` to excludes.
- Report format (fields: engine, severity, rule, file, line, match, message) is the contract for the AI fix layer — do not change without updating consumers.

## Verification gates (run after any change)

1. `npm test` → 8 passed, 0 failed (plain node asserts; gitleaks test auto-skips if binary missing).
2. Self-scan: `node bin/secflow.js scan --skip trivy` → 0 findings (repo's own secflow.yml excludes tests/).

## Hard rules

- Test fixtures use deliberately-invalid `REPLACEME` tokens (e.g. `ghp_REPLACEME_…`). NEVER add realistic fake secrets — GitHub push protection blocks the push.
- `.gitleaks.toml` allowlist stays regex-based (GitHub scans that file too).
- Zero runtime npm dependencies — Node stdlib only.
- Version lives in two places: package.json `version` and VERSION constant in bin/secflow.js. Keep in sync.

## Publishing (maintainer)

`npm publish` ships package.json `files`: bin/, action/, examples/, tests/, docs. Binary name is `secflow` (lowercase); display name is SECflow.
